observed_data: Latest full-month (2025-12-01) monthly churn rate: 6.31% total (5.10% voluntary, 1.21% involuntary). Baseline mean monthly churn: 6.67% total (5.52% voluntary). Cumulative ever-churned cohort share: 56.58% (16,975/30,000).
finding: Current monthly churn is steady at ~6.3% under normal operations; cumulative lifetime churn share is 56.6%.
hypothesis: Monthly churn rate reflects steady-state renewal attrition.
business_implication: Baseline attrition requires steady customer acquisition to sustain MRR.
recommended_action: Monitor start-of-month monthly churn rate as primary operational KPI.
how_to_test: Monthly SQL tracking against independent cohort aggregation.
caveats: Cumulative ever-churned share is a cohort total, NOT a monthly rate.

observed_data: Monthly churn peaked at 12.44% total (11.18% voluntary) in 2025-10-01 following infrastructure outage, returning to 6.31% within 60 days. Baseline voluntary churn averaged 5.52%.
finding: Churn is event-driven and sensitive to infrastructure reliability rather than undergoing secular structural decay.
hypothesis: Outage created acute spike in voluntary cancellations.
business_implication: System uptime directly protects top-line retention.
recommended_action: Establish high-availability infrastructure and disaster recovery protocols.
how_to_test: Historical event study around outage months.
caveats: Outage effect was concentrated in monthly billing accounts.

observed_data: Hazard per customer-month drops steeply by tenure: 0-3m (46.5%), 4-6m (13.9%), 7-12m (6.0%), 13+m (2.2%). Average M6 cohort retention is 69.3%.
finding: Product suffers from steep early mortality cliff in first 90 days; hazard rate drops over 20x for mature accounts.
hypothesis: Early onboarding failure drives high initial cancellation hazard.
business_implication: Interventions after Month 3 have diminishing impact compared to first 30-60 days.
how_to_test: Survival curve and cohort retention tracking.
caveats: Tenure accounts for active survival censoring.

observed_data: Average tenure of churned users is 6.0 months compared to 12.8 months for active customers.
finding: Churned customers leave early in customer lifecycle.
hypothesis: Canceled users fail to reach activation milestones.
business_implication: Churn prevention must target early lifecycle milestones.
recommended_action: Implement Day 14 and Day 30 health checks.

observed_data: Churn per customer-month is nearly identical across plans: Growth (7.41%), Scale (7.39%), Starter (7.35%). Cumulative ever-churned share: Scale (56.71%), Starter (56.70%), Growth (56.38%).
finding: Plan tier alone does not determine churn hazard when accounting for time at risk.
hypothesis: Underlying retention hazard is invariant across subscription pricing tiers.
business_implication: Do not expect higher plan tiers to automatically retain better without intervention.
recommended_action: Focus retention strategy on account value rather than assuming plan-based stickiness.
caveats: Starter has larger account volume but identical unit hazard.

observed_data: Annual billing exhibits lower churn per customer-month across all tenure bands: 0-3m (45.0% vs 47.1%), 4-6m (12.2% vs 14.6%), 7-12m (4.9% vs 6.5%), 13+m (1.9% vs 2.3%). Overall: 6.07% vs 7.86% per customer-month.
finding: Annual billing is associated with lower churn hazard at every tenure band.
hypothesis: Contract commitment and reduced renewal decision moments correlate with lower attrition.
business_implication: Shifting customers to annual contracts is associated with improved retention.
recommended_action: Incentivize annual plan conversions at month 3.
how_to_test: Stratified hazard analysis by tenure and billing cycle.
caveats: Associational finding; commitment effect may reflect customer self-selection.

observed_data: In out-of-time monthly validation (2025), inactive accounts (0 sessions in 30d) had 89.47% churn vs active at 14.05% (Relative Risk: 6.37x). Evaluated across 95 inactive accounts with 85 churners.
finding: 30-day inactivity is the strongest observable leading indicator of churn.
hypothesis: Activity cessation indicates user abandoned product workflows.
recommended_action: Trigger automated re-engagement at Day 14 before 30d cliff.
caveats: Sample size n=95 is below the 200 floor; strong directional signal but restricted to instrumented sample.

observed_data: In out-of-time monthly validation (2025), non-collaboration accounts had 24.67% churn vs collaboration accounts at 12.37% (Relative Risk: 1.99x). Evaluated across n=3,563 non-collab vs n=18,242 collab accounts.
finding: Multi-user collaboration adoption is associated with half the prospective churn hazard (2x retention moat).
hypothesis: Team workflows create operational stickiness and switching costs.
business_implication: Driving team invitations builds product defensibility.
recommended_action: Introduce mandatory team onboarding templates in first week.
caveats: Sample size meets minimum floor (n=3,563, 879 events). Associational relationship.

observed_data: When stratified by plan, channel churn per customer-month is uniform: App Store Starter (7.74%), Growth (8.15%), Scale (7.84%) vs Organic Starter (7.22%), Growth (7.24%), Scale (7.57%).
finding: App Store elevated raw churn is driven by 82.1% Starter plan skew rather than channel-specific defect.
hypothesis: Simpson's paradox / confounding by plan tier explains raw channel differences.
business_implication: Cutting App Store acquisition spend would penalize channel for demographic mix.
recommended_action: Optimize mobile onboarding rather than slashing acquisition spend.
how_to_test: Cross-stratification by channel, plan, and customer-months.
caveats: App Store acquires smaller solo users with lower initial commitment.

observed_data: Scale accounts generate 41.2% of active MRR (INR 6,553,481) from only 13.3% of active accounts (1,735 accounts, avg MRR INR 3,777). Starter generates 21.1% of MRR from 54.1% of accounts.
finding: Revenue is heavily concentrated in the top Scale tier.
hypothesis: Mid-sized teams represent the financial core of the business.
business_implication: Losing one Scale account equals losing eight Starter accounts in recurring revenue.
recommended_action: Dedicate concierge customer success strictly to Scale accounts.
caveats: Scale accounts have identical churn hazard but 8x financial exposure.

observed_data: Three revenue-at-risk measures: (1) Realized churned MRR = INR 21.00M cumulative (INR 2.29M peak in Oct 2025); (2) Exposed MRR = INR 520,212 in Medium/High tiers in instrumented cohort (INR 3.84M scaled active exposure); (3) Expected MRR at risk = INR 411,712 (estimate; 95% Wilson range: [INR 391,612, INR 432,158]).
finding: Financial risk spans historical realized losses, current portfolio exposure, and expected forward loss.
hypothesis: Different business stakeholders require distinct risk metrics (finance vs operations).
business_implication: Aligns retention budget with expected financial downside.
recommended_action: Report all three measures in executive dashboards with clear definitions.
caveats: Expected MRR at risk is an estimate based on prospective tier churn probabilities.

observed_data: Out-of-time validation across 2025 monthly snapshots: Churn rates strictly monotonic across tiers: Low 12.41% [95% CI: 11.94%-12.90%] -> Medium 22.28% [95% CI: 20.95%-23.67%] -> High 68.46% [95% CI: 60.04%-75.82%] -> Critical 100.0%. Medium (n=3,591) and Low (n=18,083) meet floor; High (n=130) and Critical (n=1) flagged for small sample size.
finding: Transparent rule-based risk framework produces strictly monotonic prospective separation out-of-time.
hypothesis: Additive behavioral friction points correlate with escalation in churn risk.
business_implication: Provides defensible triage queue for customer success operations.
recommended_action: Deploy High and Medium risk queues to CS and Support teams.
caveats: High tier n=130 has >30 events but <200 accounts; directionally robust.
